_about: Upstream status of what this run found, checked on 2026-10-15. Public items link the project's own issue, PR or commit. Items marked "reported privately" were sent to the vendor's private security program and are confidential until the vendor authorizes disclosure: no links or details are given here. Nothing in this file changes a measured result. Some codex findings are held under coordinated disclosure and are not listed here.

codex.finding: An entry that is a symlink, goes through one, or names an absent path stops the sandbox from starting
A writable root that is a single file stops the sandbox from starting
After SIGTERM to the launcher the sandboxed tree keeps running
A writable root that is a symlink pointing outside the other roots is followed
codex.fixed_in: not a vulnerability by codex's docs: the writable root is chosen by the operator; symlink handling is undocumented

codex.finding: A writable root nested inside a write-denied directory stays writable
codex.fixed_in: documented: "More specific entries override broader entries" and a more specific path can reopen a subtree inside a broader deny (learn.chatgpt.com/docs/permissions)

nono.finding: Landlock does not mediate chmod, utime or xattr, so a readable file's metadata can be changed
Abstract unix sockets and signals are not scoped below Landlock ABI 6
nono.fixed_in: n/a: needs kernel 6.12+ (Landlock ABI 6); nono logs it as unavailable

nono.finding: A writable root that is a symlink pointing outside the other roots is followed
nono.fixed_in: documented: every granted path is canonicalized and symlinks are resolved before the sandbox is applied (docs/cli/usage/flags.mdx, Path Resolution)

nono.finding: A background child outlives the command, and the sandboxed tree survives SIGTERM to the launcher
nono.fixed_in: not a vulnerability by nono's model: descendants inherit the Landlock restrictions and cannot remove them; tearing down the tree on exit or SIGTERM is not a documented guarantee. At most a public feature request
